entry.name: Levite in the Samaritan parable
entry.note: Unnamed Levite inside the narrated story in Luke 10:32, who sees the traveler and passes on the other side. Distinct from the priest immediately before him and from named Levites elsewhere.

result.appearanceFromText: The text fixes only that the Levite is a Levite who sees the wounded traveler and passes by on the other side; no physical appearance is given, so a typical Levitical man of Roman-era Judea is supplied, dressed plainly in tunic and cloak.

stages.label: Levite
stages.when: Roman Judea, first century, on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho

quotes.quote: In the same way a Levite also, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side.

stages.text: Levite in the Samaritan parable: an unnamed Jewish man of Levite lineage in his thirties to forties, of lean, moderate build, with olive-brown skin, short dark hair and a close-trimmed beard. He wears a plain undyed linen tunic and a dusty brown woollen cloak with a fringed hem, belted at the waist, and carries a small leather satchel.
